long_biography.plain_text:
The teachers who encouraged Nikita Mishin at a Moscow public school gave the future businessman an ambition to create similar opportunities for others. He established the Dar Foundation to support education, then spent years developing a school of its own. Finding a site, assembling the team and constructing the building took twelve years.

Dar funded the construction of New School in Moscow and continued to subsidise its operation. The admissions approach aimed to separate a child's prospects from the family's ability to pay: accepted pupils needing assistance could have their fees covered by the foundation. Mishin also favoured recruiting teachers for their command of a subject and enthusiasm for sharing it.

confidence.reason: His authored account explains the formative teachers, admission support and recruitment philosophy. The school independently confirms the foundation, twelve-year development, construction funding and operating subsidy.
